title: Systems Analyst, Supply Chain (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SYSTEMS ANALYST, SUPPLY CHAIN (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. As a Systems Analyst within the Starlink program you will analyze, develop, and implement tactical and strategic business processes for the supply chain group to create high impact, efficient, economical solutions. Ideal team members are highly autonomous individuals that excel in flexible environments and bring clarity and informed decision-making to our leadership teams that drive the organization.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify and analyze key performance indicators related to supply chain, especially inventory levels, lead times, supply coverage, demand fluctuations, and capacity utilization (includes developing planning models and decision-making tools)</li> <li>Create dashboards, models, and other reporting tools to enable strategic visibility across supply chain, production, cross functional teams, and leadership</li> <li>Identify inefficient workflows and develop scripts to automate tactical steps</li> <li>Track, report, and proactively manage production efficiency improvements (e.g. supply chain initiatives and process optimizations)</li> <li>Provide strategic insights and recommendations based on supply chain analysis to optimize both supplier and internal processes</li> <li>Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction, and courage</li> <li>Drive for results and customer satisfaction by collaborating with teams, leading projects and continuously spearheading improvements in supply chain</li> <li>Work with stakeholders to analyze the impact of proposed business decisions (including actual performance) on SpaceX’s business health&nbsp;</li> <li>Work with broader application software team to support ERP tools development &amp; supplier-facing portal enhancements</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree</li> <li>1+ years of experience with SQL and business intelligence tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI, Grafana) or programming softwares</li> <li>1+ years of experience in analytics, operations, management/strategy consulting, planning, or product management</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Excellent analytical skills (e.g. SQL, Tableau, PowerBI, Microsoft Office suite and similar data manipulation tools)</li> <li>Experience in python and scripting</li> <li>Degree in data science, computer science, industrial and systems engineering, operations or supply chain management</li> <li>Demonstrated success driving tangible impact/influencing within a broader organization, particularly in production or project management contexts</li> <li>Demonstrated experience managing simultaneous projects with tight deadlines and navigating ambiguous problem statements</li> <li>Proficient in understanding end user requirements, the ability to translate requirements into design requirements, and identifying system enhancement opportunities</li> <li>Ability to work both autonomously and as a team in a highly demanding, ambiguous, and fast paced environment</li> <li>Understanding of business concepts relating to supply chain management (procurement, sourcing, material movement/logistics, supplier quality, etc.)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet major milestones</li> <li>Up to 25% travel to suppliers and/or other SpaceX locations</li> <li>This position requires being on site - remote work not considered</li> </ul><div We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>The Business Operations Manager (Starlink) role sole is to enable human life on Mars and proliferate humanity’s freedom to communicate through profit improvement at SpaceX. The role combines data analytics with broader business planning, decision-making, and strategy, directly supporting SpaceX leadership. Business operations is embedded in daily operations, supporting both near-term execution and long-term planning. Team members are expected to analyze data and provide recommendations and to lead cross-functional decision-making and implementation of the recommendations. Our team is lean and dynamic, supporting several subgroups: Supply chain, engineering, manufacturing, sales, and growth. You will keep inbound, outbound, and reverse shipments moving across air, ocean, and ground, hold carriers to service and cost targets, and give the business a clear picture of status and risk before a delay hits production or a customer.</p> <p>Your focus is transportation operations, carrier relationships, and transport risk. You will manage assigned lanes and carriers, recover disruptions, support routing and rate decisions, and coordinate with suppliers, carriers, internal teams, and trade/compliance partners so freight arrives on time and in spec.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee carrier management, including daily operations, shipment flows, service quality evaluation, and performance title: Manufacturing Engineer, Supply Chain (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><span data-teams="true"><strong>MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, SUPPLY CHAIN (STARSHIP)</strong></span></p> <p>SpaceX demands a new type of supply chain. We require our suppliers to provide premium quality with rapidly evolving designs at increasingly ambitious volumes. We are actively looking for candidates who possess comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing and quality tools and have unrelenting motivation to enable suppliers for success. This position will support our Starship program and requires a combination of proven leadership and technical capabilities.</p> <p>This is a highly technical position that requires practical experience in manufacturing engineering and new product development through to stabilized production for an array of fabrication processes (components and assemblies) used in rockets and rocket engines.&nbsp;The ideal candidate will have a broad and thorough understanding of propulsion/fluid system component fabrication including extrusions, draw forming, welded and seamless tubing, cutting, and assembly, along with associated processes. This candidate should have the desire and capability to take on new challenges in unfamiliar areas to help enable our mission to Mars.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the technical point of contact for assigned parts and assemblies of the rocket, solving emergent challenges at suppliers, and mitigating risk to the manifest by addressing high-impact manufacturing and quality challenges</li> <li>Own the new product introduction of new assemblies on the rocket, including determining the ideal manufacturing method, identifying suppliers, and developing a reliable process for ramping to rate. This individual is expected to be the extreme owner for the process at suppliers for new parts, drawing changes, or when re-sourcing existing parts to a new supplier</li> <li>Conduct design for manufacturing (DFM) reviews to ensure parts are manufacturable at early stages, preferably prior to sourcing</li> <li>Work with procurement to find exceptional suppliers and vet them appropriately for quality and ability to meet our aggressive takt times</li> <li>Create and develop specifications as needed to flow down quality and manufacturing requirements to the supply base</li> <li>Scope out new forming, cutting, and inspection technologies and suppliers that may be employed to improve rate/quality/efficiency</li> <li>Review issues on assigned parts and solve to the root cause, implementing changes at the supplier, at SpaceX or both, as appropriate, drive further actions to closure, and re-source to new suppliers where appropriate</li> <li>Create and disposition issue tickets where needed, working with engineering counterparts to implement, but not limited to, required re-work, repair or use as-is disposition</li> <li>Become thoroughly familiar with your assigned parts and the processes that make up the overall assembly and become the primary point of contact for supply chain related defects on your parts</li> <li>Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction and courage to push the technical envelope which is conventionally held in the industry.</li> <li>Lead containment activities on assigned parts, working with cross-functional counterparts to agree on scope, path forward and ultimate resolution</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of experience with manufacturing and/or inspection of mechanical products in a production environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree cutting, and assembly processes, particularly in stretch forming (longitudinal and transverse), stamping (progressing and transfer), spin forming, roll forming, roll bending, press brake forming, hydroforming and tube forming/bending of primarily, but not limited to, stainless and carbon steels.</li> <li>Experience with machining and ancillary operations such as milling, turning, and tube steels is a plus</li> <li>Knowledge of supplier quality processes (production part approval process, advanced product quality planning, first article inspection reports, etc.)</li> <li>Knowledge of statistical techniques and methods, e.g., design of experiments, Lean, Six Sigma, etc.</li> <li>Experience with quality systems (ISO 9000/TS/AS9100/NADCAP) and MRP/ERP systems</li> <li>Disciplined product</li> <li>Experience in manufacturing with different grades of stainless steel</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, some nights thrives hands-on on the shop floor.&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate across diverse engineering disciplines.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed;
